pharm: Selective histamine H1-receptor antagonist with mast-cell stabilizing activity (olopatadine hydrochloride); ophthalmic and intranasal formulations
quick: Ophthalmic 0.1%: 1 drop twice daily; 0.2%/0.7%: 1 drop once daily. Nasal 0.6%: 2 sprays each nostril twice daily

summary: Olopatadine hydrochloride is a dual-acting antiallergic agent that selectively antagonizes the histamine H1 receptor and stabilizes mast cells to inhibit release of inflammatory mediators. Ophthalmic formulations (0.1% Patanol, 0.2% Pataday, 0.7% Pazeo; the 0.1% and 0.2% strengths are available OTC) treat ocular itching from allergic conjunctivitis, and the intranasal 0.6% spray (Patanase) treats allergic rhinitis symptoms. The OTC ophthalmic product temporarily relieves itchy eyes due to pollen, ragweed, grass, and animal hair and dander. Topical use produces little systemic exposure, so it is generally well tolerated, with local effects predominating; standard labeled dosing is one drop once or twice daily depending on strength, and two nasal sprays per nostril twice daily.
indications: Temporary relief of itchy eyes due to pollen, ragweed, grass, animal hair and dander (OTC ophthalmic)
Treatment of ocular itching associated with allergic conjunctivitis (ophthalmic)
Relief of the symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis (intranasal 0.6%)

admin: Ophthalmic: wash hands, tilt the head back, instill the drop into the conjunctival sac, and replace the cap after each use; do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or any surface to avoid contamination
Remove contact lenses before instilling ophthalmic olopatadine and wait at least 10 minutes before reinserting; do not wear a lens if the eye is red
If using more than one ophthalmic product, separate them by at least 5 minutes
Do not use the ophthalmic solution if it changes color or becomes cloudy
Nasal: prime the spray, insert the tip into the nostril aiming away from the septum, and spray as directed
For external/local use only; avoid contact of the ophthalmic product with internal eye structures beyond instillation
moa: Olopatadine is a selective histamine H1-receptor antagonist that also stabilizes mast cells, inhibiting the release of histamine and other inflammatory mediators that drive the allergic response. In the eye this reduces ocular itching from allergic conjunctivitis; in the nose it relieves symptoms of allergic rhinitis. Its dual antihistamine and mast-cell-stabilizing actions provide both rapid symptom relief and ongoing control of mediator release.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to olopatadine or any ingredient in the product

monitor: Eye pain or vision changes (stop and seek care)

preg: There are limited data on olopatadine in pregnancy. Because topical ophthalmic and intranasal use results in low systemic exposure, risk is expected to be low; use during pregnancy only if clearly needed and after weighing benefit against potential risk.
lact: It is not known to what extent topically applied olopatadine appears in human milk, but systemic exposure from ophthalmic or nasal use is minimal. Exercise caution in nursing women; the low systemic absorption suggests minimal infant exposure.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is required for topical ophthalmic or intranasal use given the minimal systemic absorption.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment is required for topical ophthalmic or intranasal use given the minimal systemic absorption.

minor: If using other ophthalmic products, separate instillation from olopatadine by at least 5 minutes
interactions.alcohol: No specific restriction; sedation is uncommon with topical use.
interactions.diagnostics: No clinically significant laboratory interactions are expected from topical ophthalmic or intranasal use.

missed: Apply the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule - do not double up. For the OTC once-daily ophthalmic product, do not use more than once per day.
overdose: Overdose is unlikely with topical ophthalmic or intranasal use because systemic absorption is minimal. Accidental ingestion or excessive use should be managed supportively; antihistamine overdose may cause sedation or, in young children, paradoxical excitation. Contact a poison control center if a large amount is ingested.
